items.text: Descent data and torsors
Descent data on $S'$ over $S$ = an operation of $G$ on the object over $S'$; $S'$ is a torsor under $G$ over $S$.
$S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $S'=\operatorname{Spec}k'$, $k'/k$ finite Galois with group $\Gamma$: $S'$ is a $\Gamma$-torsor over $S$ (operating on the right), and
\operatorname{Hom}_k(X,Y)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k'}(X',Y')^{\Gamma}\qquad(\text{morphisms commuting with the action of }\Gamma)
Descent data on $X'$ over $k'$ = an action of $\Gamma$ on $X'$ compatible with its action on $k'$; effective e.g. if $X'$ is quasi-projective (not always).
Infinite Galois extension: $\Gamma=\varprojlim\Gamma_i$ profinite; $\Gamma_k=\varprojlim\Gamma_{i,k}$ (affine group scheme over $k$), and $S'=\varprojlim S'_i$ is a $\Gamma_k$-torsor.
\Gamma_k(k)=\varprojlim\Gamma_i=\Gamma;\qquad \Gamma'_k\to\Gamma_k\ \ (\Gamma'=\Gamma\text{ discrete})\ \text{surjective, schematically dominant}

The action of $\Gamma_k$ on $X'$ is determined by the action of the abstract group $\Gamma$; so morphisms over $k'$ are compatible with descent data iff they commute with $\Gamma$. An action of $\Gamma$ need not come from $\Gamma_k$: then the descent data are not effective.
Families of morphisms

$S'_i\to S$ (e.g. open covering): $X\mapsto X'_i$, and $S'_i\times_SS'_j$ replaces $S'\times_SS'$. Zero-descent: a morphism $X\to Y$ is determined by the $X'_i\to Y'_i$. One-descent: compatible families $u'_i$ over $S'_i\times_SS'_j$ come from $X\to Y$. Two-descent: isomorphisms on $S'_i\times S'_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition over $S'_{ijk}$ come from an $X$.
Reduces to one morphism: $S'=\coprod S'_i$, $S'\times_SS'=\coprod S'_i\times_SS'_j$.
Gluing data, intrinsically
The double arrow $S''\rightrightarrows S'$ is universal: for $T$ over $S$ and $S$-morphisms $u,v\colon T\to S'$.
Gluing data = for all $T$ and all $u,v\colon T\to S'$ an isomorphism $u^*X'\simeq v^*X'$, compatible with pull-back along $T_1\to T$.
Descent data = such a system which is transitive ($u^*\simeq v^*\simeq w^*$): equivalently, an object over each $T$ factoring through $S'$, with $u^*X'\simeq X_T$, functorial in $T$.
The category of objects with descent data = cartesian sections of the fibred category $F$ over $C/R$ (schemes over $S$ factoring through $S'$); for a family, over the sieve it generates.
Descent and topologies

Faithfully flat quasi-compact morphisms and open coverings: properties of morphisms true after base change are true before; morphisms are determined locally; objects glue (quasi-coherent sheaves, relative affine schemes).
Effectivity of descent data = effectivity of an equivalence relation in $X'$; the quotient functor exists always. Zariski sheaves are too coarse:

\mathbb G_m\xrightarrow{\ \lambda\mapsto\lambda^n\ }\mathbb G_m=\text{quotient by }\mu_n\ \ (\text{faithfully flat, étale if }n\text{ prime to the characteristic}),\ \ \text{no local section for the Zariski topology}
A morphism $T\to S$ has a local section for the fpqc topology if it has one after a faithfully flat quasi-compact base change $S'\to S$.
The fpqc topology

A family $S'_i\to S$ covers if $S$ has an open cover by $U$ such that over each $U$ there is a finite family $U'_\alpha\to U$ with $\coprod U'_\alpha\to U$ faithfully flat, quasi-compact, surjective, each $U'_\alpha\to U$ factoring through some $S'_i$.
Coverings are transitive and stable under base change: the category of schemes is a site.
A presheaf $F$ (contravariant functor to sets) is a sheaf for a covering $S_i\to S$ if
F(S)\longrightarrow\prod_iF(S_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}F(S_i\times_SS_j)\quad\text{exact}
Enough to check: open coverings, and a single faithfully flat quasi-compact $S'\to S$.
Sheaves on a site behave as on a space: epimorphisms are effective and stable under base change, sums distributive, base change commutes with direct limits.
